title: Origins of early Christianity
summary: Christianity emerged in the first century CE from a small sect of Second Temple Judaism. In the Acts account, the first community formed in Jerusalem around Pentecost, when about three thousand people were baptised; one essay says it was led by Jesus's family. Gentile converts later became the majority. Acts is religious tradition, so the early details are debated.

uncertainty.note: Sources place the crucifixion between 26 and 36 CE; the Apostolic Council c. 49 CE; gentile converts dominated by the end of the century. Start year 30 is the id marker only.

importance.justification: The beginning of what became a major world religion, in a Jewish setting.

related.because: The movement began among followers of Jesus after his death.
Disciples began preaching after Jesus was crucified.
